name: com.envisioning/ncb
title: National Capability Benchmark
description: Country capability scores with their confidence, for 135 countries and nine dimensions. Read-only.

tools.name: list_dimensions
tools.description: The nine capability dimensions, the question each one answers, and how many indicators each has: scored, declared gaps, rejected, and conditions published beside it. Also the dataset version and the quoting contract. Start here.

tools.name: get_country
tools.description: One country's nine dimensions, each with score, confidence and its band, indicator count, coverage flag, trend, panel estimate where one exists, and links to the known limits that apply. Takes an ISO3 code or an English country name.

indicators.description: Add every observed indicator row: value, year and source

tools.name: compare_countries
tools.description: Two to 4 countries side by side on the nine dimensions, in the order you give them. The result is not sorted by score: the benchmark compares shapes and does not rank (D1).

tools.name: get_stories
tools.description: Computed descriptive stories for any country in the frame (D192): shape_mirror (nearest capability profiles across the frame), peer_contrast (farthest shape among the 10 nearest income peers) and peer_standing (each dimension against the income-peer median, keeping thin-evidence dimensions out of headlines). Every score carries its confidence, band, indicator count, coverage flag and known limits.

story.description: One story id (shape_mirror, peer_contrast, peer_standing); omit for all available stories

tools.name: search_indicators
tools.description: Search the registry of indicators by words in the name or definition, and filter by dimension or status: scored, gap (no adequate dataset yet), rejected (a dataset exists and the project disqualified it) or condition (published beside a dimension, never scored).

tools.name: get_decision
tools.description: Read one entry of the decision record by number, for example D1 or D118: the methodological choice, why it was made, what it costs and what evidence would overturn it. Use it to answer "why does the benchmark do X?".

tools.name: get_limit
tools.description: Read one known limit by id (A1, A2, ...): a place where the model produces a number that is wrong about the world. get_country lists the ids that apply to each score. Without an id, lists every limit with the dimensions and countries it covers.
